VERDANA TECHNOLOGIES, INC.
COMPENSATION AUTHORITY POLICY
Version 3.2.  
Board-Approved: January 15, 2025
Confidential — Internal Governance Document
Verdana Technologies, Inc. 3200 Brazos Ridge Parkway, Suite 800 Austin, TX 78745
EIN: 84-3921057
Right-click to update Table of Contents
Article 1 — Purpose and Scope
Section 1.1 — Statement of Purpose. The purpose of this Compensation Authority Policy (the "Policy") is to establish maximum compensation authority parameters ("CAP Limits") for all executive-level employment offers, employment agreements, retention packages, and severance arrangements entered into by Verdana Technologies, Inc. ("Verdana" or the "Company"), a Delaware C-Corporation headquartered in Austin, Texas. This Policy sets forth the framework within which the Company's management, People Operations function, and external advisors must operate when structuring, negotiating, and finalizing compensation arrangements for senior executives, and defines the escalation procedures required when proposed arrangements would exceed the limits established herein.
Section 1.2 — Scope of Application. This Policy applies to all offers, employment agreements, retention packages, severance arrangements, and any other compensation-related commitments made to individuals being recruited for, promoted into, or currently occupying positions at the following executive levels across all divisions, subsidiaries, and affiliates of the Company:
(a) Vice President ("VP");
(b) Senior Vice President ("SVP"); and
(c) C-Suite (Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, Chief Technology Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief People Officer, Chief Revenue Officer, Chief Legal Officer, and any other officer holding a "Chief" title or equivalent designation as determined by the Board of Directors).
For avoidance of doubt, this Policy governs compensation commitments made both to external candidates and to internal employees being promoted or renegotiating existing arrangements.
Section 1.3 — Supersession. This Policy supersedes all prior compensation authority policies, memoranda, guidelines, and related governance documents of the Company, including without limitation CAP v.3.1 (approved September 12, 2024) and all earlier versions. To the extent that any previously approved employment arrangement contains terms that were authorized under a prior version of this Policy, such terms shall remain in effect for the duration of the applicable employment agreement, but any modification, extension, or renegotiation of such terms shall be governed by this Policy.
Section 1.4 — Binding Effect. This Policy is binding on all Company officers, members of the People Operations function (including recruiters, compensation analysts, and human resources business partners), hiring managers at every level, and any external advisors, executive search firms, or legal counsel engaged by the Company to negotiate employment terms on behalf of Verdana. No individual subject to this Policy may commit the Company to any compensation term that exceeds the applicable CAP Limit without obtaining the requisite approval in accordance with Article 4.
Section 1.5 — Policy Objectives. The objectives of this Policy are as follows:
(a) Consistency. To ensure that executive compensation decisions are made within a consistent and transparent framework, reducing the risk of ad hoc commitments that may create internal equity concerns or set unintended precedents.
(b) Fiduciary Prudence. To ensure that the Company's compensation commitments are consistent with sound fiduciary principles, particularly in light of the Company's obligations t

{"id": 312, "title": "Ashworth Kane — Confidential candidate assessment", "doc_type": "agreement_document", "related_shape": "lab-employment-compensation-escalation", "body": "[Source: Harvey LAB, ashworth-kane-candidate-assessment.docx — extracted verbatim]

ASHWORTH KANE PARTNERS, LLC
150 North Wacker Drive, Suite 2600, Chicago, IL 60606
CONFIDENTIAL CANDIDATE ASSESSMENT
 
Prepared for: Verdana Technologies, Inc.
Engagement: SVP, Product Engineering — Autonomous Analytics Division
Candidate: Dr. Mariana Chen-Velasco
Prepared by: Ashworth Kane Partners, LLC
Date: May 30, 2025
Classification: Confidential — Restricted Distribution
I. Engagement Overview and Search Summary
Ashworth Kane Partners, LLC ("Ashworth Kane" or the "Firm") was retained by Verdana Technologies, Inc. ("Verdana" or the "Company") in October 2024 to conduct a confidential executive search for the inaugural Senior Vice President, Product Engineering — Autonomous Analytics Division (the "Role"). The engagement was authorized by Priya Ramanathan, Chief People Officer, with the concurrence of Verdana's Chief Executive Officer and, subsequently, the Board of Directors' Compensation Committee. This assessment is furnished in connection with that engagement and presents Ashworth Kane's recommendation regarding the candidacy of Dr. Mariana Chen-Velasco.
Engagement Economics. The engagement was structured as a fixed retainer of $175,000, fully earned upon execution of the search engagement agreement, plus a placement fee equal to 25% of the placed candidate's Year 1 total cash compensation (defined as base salary plus target annual bonus). The retainer has been earned in full. The placement fee will be due upon the candidate's acceptance of a fully authorized employment offer from Verdana.
Search Objective. The primary objective of the engagement is to identify and deliver a senior technical executive capable of building and scaling a net-new product division within Verdana's enterprise SaaS platform. The Role reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer and carries accountability for the Board-approved first-year revenue target of $14,000,000 and the three-year revenue plan of $62,000,000 for the Autonomous Analytics division. The successful candidate must combine deep technical expertise in autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and machine learning with a demonstrated track record of standing up revenue-generating product organizations at enterprise scale. The Board further specified that the ideal candidate should possess the executive presence, market credibility, and investor-readiness profile appropriate for a company that may pursue an initial public offering or strategic transaction within the next 18 to 24 months, as indicated by Ridgeline Partners, Inc., Verdana's lead financial advisor.
Scope of Search. The search was national in scope with targeted international outreach to select markets, including Toronto, London, and Bangalore, where concentrations of relevant talent were identified during the research phase. The Firm's proprietary research function surveyed the enterprise AI/ML, autonomous systems, and advanced analytics product leadership landscape, with particular emphasis on candidates drawn from enterprise SaaS companies in the $1 billion to $3 billion valuation range and adjacent technology sectors, including infrastructure-layer AI/ML platform companies and vertical analytics providers serving regulated industries.
Duration. The search has been active for approximately seven months, from October 2024 through the date of this assessment in May 2025. This duration reflects the highly specialized nature of the role, the limited pool of qualified candidates who combine the requisite technical depth with division-building experience, and the competitive market dynamics that have characterized senior AI/ML leadership hiring throughout the 2024–2025 cycle.
Candidate Pipeline Sum
